findings.text: action_form drops every option that is not in _ACTION_OPTION_PARAM rather than refusing the command, so the action it prints beside a commitless promotion is not the printed command: reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1653 composes `reckon crew complete --run X --gate not-run --no-commit '<why the run produced no commit>' --outcome '<what the run produced>'`, and action_form renders that as `crew(action="complete", run_id="X", gate="not-run", outcome="<what the run produced>")` with no `no_commit`; a coordinator following the offered action runs a promotion that lacks the declaration the commitless run is promoted under and is refused. Rendered against the real function in the node's own tree, the value is exactly that string.

a repeated option appends the same parameter name twice, so a run carrying two commits renders `crew(action="complete", run_id="X", gate="passed", commits="1111111", commits="2222222")` — a duplicate keyword argument, which is not a callable form for the surface the field is offered as. reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1660 appends one `--commit` per commit, so any promotion duty for a run with more than one commit is affected. Verified by running action_form on that literal command in the node's tree.

the added `next_action` on a duty row carries the MCP action form, while `next_action` is an established key elsewhere in the repository for a CLI command string — reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1564 produces it and reckon/crew/obligations.py:397 itself reads a recovery row's `next_action` as the duty's `next_command`. The same key now names two different kinds of value, and a reader that knows the established meaning will read the action form as a command. No consumer reads the duty row's `next_action` as a command today, so this is a readability hazard rather than a live break.

`from reckon.crew import obligations as obligations_module  # noqa: F401` is unused by reckon/mcp.py; the obligations view is dispatched in reckon/mcp_crew_views.py (reckon/mcp_views.py:3818). It was added so tests/test_mcp_crew_obligations.py:44 can read `mcp_module.obligations_module`, which fixes a real pre-existing collection error but leaves production code carrying an import that exists only for a test. The surrounding writer of the obligations view is reckon/mcp_views.py, which is outside this node's fence, so the in-fence fix is understandable and is recorded in the manifest's evidence_inputs.

the same eight action names are declared three times by one change: reckon/mcp.py:2109 `_WRITE_ACTIONS`, reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py:30 `CREW_WRITE_ACTIONS` and reckon/crew/obligations.py:122 `_ACTION_VERBS`. reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py is the owner of the set (it is the module that dispatches on it), and the other two could read it; four copies of one list are what a later ninth action has to be remembered in.
